title: Coefficient representatives with a common generic differential basis
statement: Let $(B,\mathfrak n)$ be a reduced complete Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] of characteristic $p>0$, equidimensional of finite dimension $e\geq1$ (meaning $\dim(B/\mathfrak q)=e$ for every minimal prime $\mathfrak q$) [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], with residue field $k$. Optionally fix a perfect subfield $k_0\subseteq B$, meaning that $x\mapsto x^p$ is bijective on $k_0$. There exist a field section $s:k\hookrightarrow B$ of the residue map and $a_1,\ldots,a_e\in\mathfrak n$ such that, for every minimal prime $\mathfrak q$, the images of $\mathrm da_1,\ldots,\mathrm da_e$ form a basis of $\widehat\Omega_{B/k}\otimes_B\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak q)$. The $k$-algebra structure is $s$; $\widehat\Omega_{B/k}:=\varprojlim_m\Omega_{B/k}/\mathfrak n^m\Omega_{B/k}$, where $\Omega$ is the module of Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. When $k_0$ was fixed, $s$ restricts to the given inclusion of $k_0$ (identified with its image in $k$).

source.place: Expose IV, 2.1.4–2.1.11 (coefficient representatives and generic rank e), 2.1.9–2.1.10 and first paragraph of 2.1.12 (common exact differential basis, moved into the maximal ideal by pth powers); compatibility with a perfect subfield follows from 2.1.4 since its elements have unique compatible p-power roots.

proof.text: Choose a $p$-basis $(b_i)_{i\in E}$ of the residue field $k$ using [lem-weil-pbc-p-basis-exists]. Choose arbitrary lifts $\beta_i\in B$. By [lem-per-prescribed-pbasis-coefficient-section] they lie in a coefficient field $\kappa\subset B$. The minimal primes are a finite list $\mathfrak q_1,\ldots,\mathfrak q_c$ by [lem-sc-finite-minimal-primes-over-ideal] with ideal $(0)$. Put $A_j=B/\mathfrak q_j$ and $L_j=\operatorname{Frac}(A_j)$. Each $A_j$ is a complete local domain by the quotient assertion of [lem-per-completed-differential-finite-conormal], and has dimension $e$ by the hypothesis. The image of $\kappa$ in every $A_j$ is still a coefficient field.

source.place: 2.1.4 and 2.1.6; EGA 0_IV 20.7.8 for completeness of the quotients

proof.text: For finite $J\subset E$ put $F_J=\kappa^p(\beta_i\mid i\notin J)$. The monomial basis in [lem-weil-pbc-p-basis-complement-monomial-basis] gives $[\kappa:F_J]=p^{|J|}$. Apply [lem-per-cofinite-pbasis-completed-generic-rank] to each $A_j$, and take the union of the finitely many exceptional sets. Choose a finite $J$ containing this union, and put $r=|J|$, $F=F_J$ and $M=M_F(B)$. By [lem-per-completed-differential-finite-conormal], $M$ is finite, the exact differentials generate it, and its generic fibre $V_j=M\otimes_B L_j$ identifies with that for $A_j$. Thus $\dim_{L_j}V_j=e+r$ for every $j$.

Here is the ideal-spanning calculation used twice below. In any $A_j$, let $I$ be a nonzero ideal and choose $0\neq u\in I$. In its generic differential space the identity $d(au)=a\,du+u\,da$ gives $da=u^{-1}(d(au)-a\,du)$ for every $a\in A_j$. Both $u$ and $au$ belong to $I$. Since the exact differentials generate by [lem-per-completed-differential-finite-conormal], the vectors $df$ for $f\in I$ span the generic differential space. This is the entire argument of the source's ideal-spanning lemma.

We will also use this elementary linear selection argument. If $W$ spans a vector space $V$ with $\dim V\geq n$, then for any $v_1,\ldots,v_n$ one can choose $w_i\in W\cup\{0\}$ with the $v_i+w_i$ independent. Induct on $n$: make the first $n-1$ independent, with span $U$. If $v_n\notin U$, take $w_n=0$; otherwise choose $w_n\in W\setminus U$, possible since $\dim U=n-1<\dim V$. The case $n=0$ is empty.

source.place: 2.1.10, with the omitted induction written out

proof.text: Enumerate $J$ as $1,\ldots,r$. We construct lifts $\gamma_i$ of $b_i$, $i\in J$, whose differentials are independent in the first $j$ generic fibres, by induction on $j$. At $j=0$ use $\gamma_i=\beta_i$. At the step to $j+1$, let $Q=B$ if $j=0$, and $Q=\bigcap_{h\leq j}\mathfrak q_h$ otherwise. The image $I$ of $Q\cap\mathfrak n$ in $A_{j+1}$ is nonzero: choose $t\in\mathfrak n\setminus\mathfrak q_{j+1}$ (the quotient has positive dimension), and, for each $h\leq j$, choose $u_h\in\mathfrak q_h\setminus\mathfrak q_{j+1}$. Then $t\prod_hu_h\in Q\cap\mathfrak n$ has nonzero image. By the preceding ideal calculation and linear selection, choose $m_i\in Q\cap\mathfrak n$ so that $d\gamma_i+dm_i$ are independent in $V_{j+1}$; the dimension is $e+r\geq r$. Replace $\gamma_i$ by $\gamma_i+m_i$. Their residues are unchanged, and on each earlier component $m_i$ maps to zero, so its differential is zero under the generic quotient identification of [lem-per-completed-differential-finite-conormal]. The previously obtained independence is preserved. This proves the induction.

Set $\gamma_i=\beta_i$ for $i\notin J$, and keep the final lifts from the preceding induction for $i\in J$. Apply [lem-per-prescribed-pbasis-coefficient-section] to this entire family of lifts. It gives a coefficient section $s:k\to B$ with image $\kappa'$, whose $p$-basis is $(\gamma_i)_{i\in E}$. This constructs $\kappa'$ without assuming that it contains the old $\kappa^p$. The displayed subfield formula in 2.1.11 is not used; the report gives a counterexample to that formula.

source.place: 2.1.4 applied to the perturbed lifts of 2.1.8; correction of the displayed formula in 2.1.11

proof.text: For any $B$-module $N$ and any derivation $D:B\to N$ over $\mathbf F_p$, one has $D(x^p)=0$. Finite $p$-monomial expansions in a coefficient field therefore show that $D$ kills $F=\kappa^p(\beta_i\mid i\notin J)$ exactly when it kills all the $\beta_i$ with $i\notin J$. Likewise it kills $\kappa'$ exactly when it kills all the $\gamma_i$. As these two families coincide off $J$, being a $\kappa'$-derivation is equivalent to being an $F$-derivation with $D\gamma_i=0$ for $i\in J$. These assertions follow term by term from the Leibniz rule, including inverses via $D(x^{-1})=-x^{-2}D(x)$.

source.place: 2.1.11: the corrected coefficient-change argument using the p-basis expansion

proof.text: Let $U$ be the $B$-submodule of $M=M_F(B)$ generated by the $r$ vectors $d_F\gamma_i$, $i\in J$. Both $M/U$ and $M_{\kappa'}(B)$ are finite by [lem-per-completed-differential-finite-conormal]. They are complete by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian]. The preceding derivation calculation and the universal property in [lem-per-completed-differential-finite-conormal] give inverse canonical maps $M/U\leftrightarrows M_{\kappa'}(B)$: both maps carry the class of $d_Fa$ to $d_{\kappa'}a$, and their composites are identities since exact differentials generate. On tensoring with $L_j$ this quotient has dimension $(e+r)-r=e$, since the $d_F\gamma_i$ were independent in $V_j$. Hence $M'=M_{\kappa'}(B)$ has generic rank $e$ on every component.

source.place: 2.1.11, generic-rank conclusion; EGA 0_IV 20.7.14 for the universal property

proof.text: Apply the same finite induction on components to obtain $f_1,\ldots,f_e\in B$ with $d_{\kappa'}f_i$ a basis on every component. Start with all $f_i=0$ and no processed components. At the next component use the ideal $I=\operatorname{im}(Q\cap\mathfrak n\to A_{j+1})\neq0$ constructed above. Its exact differentials span by the earlier ideal calculation, now with coefficient field $\kappa'$, using [lem-per-completed-differential-finite-conormal]. The linear selection argument with $n=e$ makes the next $e$ differentials independent by adding lifts from $Q\cap\mathfrak n$. Their images, and thus their differentials, vanish on all processed components; the generic quotient identification of the same cited node preserves the earlier bases. All the generic spaces have dimension $e$, so independence is a basis. At the end the same $e$ elements work on every component.

source.place: first paragraph of 2.1.12, spelling out its reference to the preceding induction

proof.text: For completeness one may move this tuple into $\mathfrak n$ exactly as in the source. For each $j$ choose $t_j\in\mathfrak n\setminus\mathfrak q_j$ and $v_j\in\bigcap_{h\neq j}\mathfrak q_h\setminus\mathfrak q_j$; the latter is the product of elements of $\mathfrak q_h\setminus\mathfrak q_j$, with empty product $1$. Then $h=\sum_jt_jv_j$ belongs to $\mathfrak n$ and has nonzero image modulo each $\mathfrak q_j$, since all summands except the $j$th vanish there. Put $a_i=h^pf_i\in\mathfrak n$. The Leibniz rule gives $d_{\kappa'}a_i=h^pd_{\kappa'}f_i$, because $d_{\kappa'}(h^p)=0$. Multiplication by this nonzero scalar on each generic fibre preserves a basis, giving precisely the requested $a_i$.

source.place: first paragraph of 2.1.12, multiplication by pth powers; explicit finite avoidance construction

proof.text:
If a perfect subfield $k_0\subseteq B$ was specified, its reduction is injective, since a nonzero field element is a unit. For $c\in k_0$ and every $m\geq1$, choose $c_m\in k_0$ with $c_m^{p^m}=c$. The difference $c_m-s(\overline{c_m})$ lies in $\mathfrak n$, so in characteristic $p$,
$$c-s(\bar c)=\bigl(c_m-s(\overline{c_m})\bigr)^{p^m}\in\mathfrak n^{p^m}.$$
The intersection of these powers is zero by [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Thus $s(\bar c)=c$ for every $c\in k_0$. This proves the optional compatibility for the section already constructed.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NH-d82cc58ca (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read ILO IV 2.1.1–2.1.12 with Prop. 1.2.4, and EGA 0_IV 20.7.14, 20.7.15, 20.7.20 and 21.9.1. The item statement is unchanged. All 11 steps check out against the cited statements. Source error confirmed: the field κ' := κ^p(β_i; β'_i) in ILO 2.1.11 contains m^p, a nonzero element of the maximal ideal, so it cannot be a subfield of A. Example: F_p(u)[[t]] with β' = u+t gives t^p ∈ κ'. The repair is correct: it takes the unique coefficient field containing the final lifts (ILO 2.1.4), and Step 7 shows that a κ'-derivation is the same as an F-derivation that kills the γ_i. Step 8 builds inverse maps M/U ⇄ M_{κ'}(B) from the universal property and gets generic rank (e+r)−r = e. Step 5 lifts corrections into Q∩n, which keeps residues unchanged; the source's lift into q_j does not. Steps 10 and 11 (h^p trick, perfect subfield through n^{p^m}) are correct. All three new nodes are true and strictly smaller than the item. (1) prescribed-pbasis-section is Bourbaki AC IX §2 Th. 1(a), as ILO 2.1.4 cites it; tested on F_p(u+t) ⊂ F_p(u)[[t]]. (2) cofinite generic rank is ILO (2.b) with the 'every J ⊇ J_0' form from Prop. 1.2.4. Tested on κ[[x]], and on κ[[x,y]]/(y^p − u x^p): rank 2 at J = ∅ and 1+1 at J = {u}, which shows the exceptional set is needed. (3) completed conormal follows from EGA 20.7.14, 20.7.15 and 20.7.20; the image of the finite I/I² is closed, and (q/q²)_q = 0 for a reduced ring at a minimal prime. Duplicate search: the trf continuous-differential nodes cover power-series presentations only, the sibling lem-per-finite-formal-map-differential-cokernel is a different sequence, and the blueprint has nothing. Tool uses accepted (generic field theory and commutative algebra): lem-weil-pbc-p-basis-exists, lem-weil-pbc-p-basis-complement-monomial-basis, lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian. Advisory only: the new nodes list lem-weil-pbc-p-basis-exists in stmt_deps for the notion 'p-basis', as existing pbc nodes do. No SGA cited. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem coefficient_field_generic_differential_basis (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsLocalRing B] [IsReduced B] [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B) B] [CharP B p] (e : ℕ) (he : 1 ≤ e) (hequidim : ∀ q : Ideal B, IsMinimalPrime q → ringKrullDim (B ⧸ q) = (e : WithBot ℕ∞)) (K₀ : Type v) [Field K₀] (constants : Option (K₀ →+* B)) (hperfect : ∀ ι : K₀ →+* B, constants = some ι → Function.Bijective (fun x : K₀ ↦ x ^ p)) : ∃ (s : IsLocalRing.ResidueField B →+* B) (a : Fin e → B), (IsLocalRing.residue B).comp s = RingHom.id (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B) ∧ (∀ i : Fin e, a i ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B) ∧ CoefficientSectionGenericDifferentialBasis B e s a ∧ (∀ ι : K₀ →+* B, constants = some ι → ∀ x : K₀, s (IsLocalRing.residue B (ι x)) = ι x)
